body_ar:
حكم أخذ الأجرة على قسم التركة ما الحكم الشرعي في مسألة شائعة في بلادنا وهي أن فقهاء بلدنا لا يقسمون التركة إلا بعد أن يأخذوا نصيبهم من المال قبل أن يقسم، فمثلا يأخذون من الإبل بعيرا ومن البقر جذعة ويقولون بأن هذا حق شرعي لهم علما بأن الورثة قد يكون من بينهم أيتام صغار فهل لهم حق في المال أم لا؟

أن الله سبحانه وتعالى حرم مال المسلم كتحريمه لنفسه، فقد صح عن النبي (ص) أنه قال: «فإن دماءكم وأموالكم وأعراضكم عليكم حرام كحرمة يومكم هذا في بلدكم هذا في شهركم هذا» وقال: «حرمة مال المسلم كحرمة دمه» فلذلك لا يحل أخذ مال امرئ مسلم إلا عن طيبة نفس منه، وهذا من المعلوم من الدين بالضرورة، فلا يحل لأولئك القوم أن يأخذوا من مال اليتامى ولا من مال الذين يقسمون لهم التركات شيئا إلا برضاهم..
body_en:
The ruling on taking a fee for dividing an estate. What is the ruling of the Sharia on a matter that is widespread in our country, namely that the jurists of our country will not divide an estate until they have taken their share of the property before it is divided — so, for example, they take a camel from the camels and a young cow from the cattle, and they say that this is a right the Sharia gives them — bearing in mind that among the heirs there may be young orphans? Have they a right in the property or not?

God, glorified and exalted, has made the property of a Muslim inviolable just as He has made his person inviolable. It is soundly established from the Prophet, upon whom be peace, that he said: "Your blood and your property and your honour are inviolable to one another, like the inviolability of this day of yours, in this land of yours, in this month of yours." And he said: "The inviolability of a Muslim's property is like the inviolability of his blood." For that reason it is not lawful to take the property of a Muslim man except with his willing consent, and this is among the things necessarily known to be part of the religion. So it is not lawful for those people to take anything from the property of the orphans, nor from the property of those for whom they divide estates, except with their consent..

options: has made the property of a Muslim inviolable just as He has made his person inviolable
has forbidden [taking] the property of a Muslim as He has forbidden [taking] his life
has made a Muslim's wealth sacrosanct as He has made his self sacrosanct
flags.note: Ḥarrama here is used of an inviolability attaching to a thing, the sense carried through the passage by ḥurmah in the hadith, rather than of a prohibition attaching to an act. Option 1 converts it into the five-rulings sense of ḥarām, which would make the sentence say something narrower than the Arabic. Nafs is the person or life, not 'soul' in this idiom.

flags.context: فمثلا يأخذون من الإبل بعيرا ومن البقر جذعة
options: a jadhaʿah [a beast in its second or third year]
flags.note: Jadhaʿah is an age-grade term from the law of zakat and sacrifice, and its exact age differs by animal and by school — for cattle it is generally in the third year, for sheep in the second. Since the questioner is describing what the local jurists take as their fee, the precise grade matters to the sum involved. Option 1 keeps the Arabic and gives a range rather than asserting one age.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.

In the source, the answer begins with the elliptical particle 'anna ('[the answer is] that ...'), the Joomla fatwa template's standing form. The English drops the particle and begins the sentence directly; no content is added or removed by this.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off with a double dot and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

The Sheikh does give a ruling within the published excerpt — that the practice is not lawful without the heirs' consent — so this record is not marked critical_for_display. But the excerpt stops before he addresses the second limb of the question, whether a fee for the work of dividing may lawfully be charged at all, which is a distinct question from taking it unilaterally beforehand. A reviewer should not treat the excerpt as his complete position on remuneration for this service.

'Among the things necessarily known to be part of the religion' renders min al-maʿlūm min al-dīn bi-l-ḍarūrah, a technical expression for a matter so well established that ignorance of it is not excused. Ḍarūrah here does not carry the glossary's sense of 'necessity' as a legal threshold.
The first hadith is from the Farewell Sermon; the Sheikh does not name a collection for either report, and none has been supplied.
